newsitem.title: UK: UK actuaries warn investors may overpay for TEPs.
newsitem.headline: UK actuaries warn investors may overpay for TEPs.

text.p: The Faculty & Institute of Actuaries on Tuesday warned UK financial watchdog the Personal Investment Authority (PIA) that investors may be being tempted into overpaying for second hand traded endowment policies (TEPs).
It said that information currently provided may lead investors to have unreasonable expectations of the eventual returns on policies.
In a letter to PIA chief executive Colette Bowe, the Faculty & Institute of Actuaries said the current approach used to assess the long-term value of TEPs was the main problem.
Rising investor demand means that many policies are trading at prices which do not appear justifiable at a time when both annual and terminal bonus rates remain under severe pressure, it said.
Duncan Ferguson of the Faculty said that they believed investors may currently be overpaying.
"We are therefore urging the PIA, which is now undertaking a major review of the TEPs market, to improve the information given to investors," said Ferguson.

"In our view this should include the PIA requiring potential purchasers to be given the official PIA policy projections, which are generally based on the current asset share and have regard to the office's intended smoothing method."
The traditioonal average discount rate approach prices TEPs by projecting the maturity value of the contract on the assumption current bonus rates remain unchanged.
Several life companies have given warnings over the past few years about the difficulties of maintaining bonus rates on endowments written in the 1980s, said the Faculty.
The alternative asset share method tends to be more accurate because it does not use discount rates, which rely on a projection of unknown future investment returns, it added.
